messages.subject: Specifying home directory for JGR
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
Apologies if this has been answered elsewhere but I couldn't find a solution
to my question on previous threads.

My question relates to setting a home directory, preferably before an
install of JGR. I ask as on install and running, JGR sets the directory to
the C:\Users\users folder and then saves the JGRprefsrc & JGREditorprefsrc
into this folder. I would rather these files be saved just about anywhere
else but here (it is a high traffic folder and the loss/accidental moving of
my preference files has caused me headaches in the past). 

So I tried the basic thing of changing the default working directory through
Edit -> Preferences -> General -> Default working directory. In this case, a
new set of JGRprefsrc & JGREditorprefsrc files is formed where I set the
directory but if I then delete the original JGRprefsrc/JGREditorprefsrc
files, I again lose my preferences (and the default working directory is
reset back to the user folder). 

Thinking I could specify a home directory before installation I've tried
creating the launchJGR.bat file with the following specifications, then
installing:
set R_HOME=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3
set R_LIBS=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3\library
set R_LIBS_USER=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3\library
jgr.exe --rhome=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3 --libpath=C:\Program
Files\R\R-2.15.3\library

But to no avail, the preference files are still created in the User file. 

And yes I'm aware it isn't good saving packages in the Program Files tree,
I'm just working on the preferences problem first!

Using Windows 7 Home 64-bit, R version 2.15.3 and JGR v1.7.16.

Thank you for your time!

> Edit -> Preferences -> General -> Default working directory. In this case, a
> new set of JGRprefsrc & JGREditorprefsrc files is formed where I set the
> directory but if I then delete the original JGRprefsrc/JGREditorprefsrc
> files, I again lose my preferences (and the default working directory is
> reset back to the user folder). 
> 
> Thinking I could specify a home directory before installation I've tried
> creating the launchJGR.bat file with the following specifications, then
> installing:
> set R_HOME=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3
> set R_LIBS=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3\library
> set R_LIBS_USER=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3\library
> jgr.exe --rhome=C:\Program Files\R\R-2.15.3 --libpath=C:\Program
> Files\R\R-2.15.3\library
> 
> But to no avail, the preference files are still created in the User file. 
> 

It's a chicken-and-egg probelm: in order to read the preferences JGR has to read the file from a well-known place. Once it can read the preferences it will know that you want to move them to another place, but it cannot really do so before reading them. That's why the preferences are always first read from your home.

That said, you can always set HOME to direct the launcher to another directory to load the preferences from. However, I think that only applies to the launcher, not necessarily JGR itself so that's something that could be improved.

Cheers,
Simon

Well, I found the issue: it is using the 64-bit versions of R/JGR. 
I installed the 32-bit versions of both and had them both working within
minutes.

To anyone else who has this problem using the 64-bit versions, use the
32-bit ones instead if you need JGR to work.

Developers: Is there a possibility of working around this compatibility
issue in the next release (given the amount of similiar posts on google you
get for it when searching for this problem it would seem that it isn't
uncommon). 

Thanks.

... assuming you don't have a full 64-bit R + Java chain?


> Developers: Is there a possibility of working around this compatibility
> issue in the next release (given the amount of similiar posts on google you
> get for it when searching for this problem it would seem that it isn't
> uncommon). 
> 

I don't see any such issues reported here. Some people rely on google for answers which fails miserably on non-mainstream topic, because there are too many wrong answers from people that have no idea what they are talking about. 

Anyway, I don't see the full context. The way you start JGR is to download the launcher and run it. It should work automatically with the standard setup and write-permissions in the R library. You have to have matching architecture of R, Java and packages. Most common mistake (if you look at the archives) is people using 64-bit R and 32-bit Java or vice versa. If you have some issue that has not been covered, please supply details about exact failure, your setup and versions involved (R, Java, packages) so we can try to reproduce it.

Thanks,
Simon
